newsitem.title: GERMANY: SMH says to stay part of Lloyds for time being.
newsitem.headline: SMH says to stay part of Lloyds for time being.

text.p: Lloyds TSB Group Plc's German banking unit Schroeder, Muenchmeyer Hengst & Co (SMH) said on Friday it would not break with its U.K. parent at least until its current restructuring plan was complete.

The unit, which has been at the centre of speculation that Lloyds wanted to sell it to a Swiss bank, said it had held talks with unnamed potential partners but had decided to remain as part of the British group for the time being.
Lloyds fully supported this decision, SMH said.

"These talks (with other banks) ended with the conviction that it is in the interests of SMH's clients, staff and owners to continue its restructuring as planned and bring 1997 to a successful end," the statement said.

Lloyds owns 96 percent of SMH, having come to its rescue in the 1980s after one of the German bank's major corporate clients collapsed. It has so far declined comment on the speculation surrounding SMH.

SMH, which last year announced plans to step out of lending activities to focus on institutional brokerage, asset management and retail securities business, said 1996 had been a successful year in terms of its restructuring.
The same was true of profitability in these core areas.
Looking ahead, SMH said it planned to step up its international securities activities via co-operations with other firms, having already set up a European network of such partners.
